_doc: Single source of truth for the KELOR mascot. Read by scripts/assets/validate.mjs (phase 1), scripts/blender/* (phase 3) and the R3F runtime (phase 2+). Validated by src/lib/character/schema.ts in tests. Change values here, never hard-code them elsewhere. Bump contractVersion on breaking changes.

meta._doc: Coordinate system follows glTF: metres, +Y up, the character faces +Z (towards the default camera). Left side (_L) is +X. Origin sits between the feet on the ground plane.
meta.name: Kelo

files._doc: Output paths of the asset pipeline, relative to the repo root. Served from public/ on Vercel's CDN (D-052).

budgets._doc: Hard limits enforced by pnpm validate:model. lite is the first-paint model and the low-tier model; full streams in afterwards. File sizes are compressed (Meshopt geometry; WebP on lite, KTX2 on full). Lite keeps its phase 4 budget; full returned to 1500 kB in phase 6 for a 2048 px base colour and a 1024 px normal map, since it streams in after first paint; since phones keep lite, full is the desktop model, and the phase 8 polish raised it to 3600 kB and 60000 triangles for twice the density and a 2048 px normal map carrying the scales. Draw calls = mesh primitives rendered once (shadow passes excluded).

skeleton._doc: Exact bone names and hierarchy. restHead is the nominal bone head position in metres for a 1.2 m character; phase 2 builds the placeholder rig from it and phase 3 refits it to the real mesh landmarks. Procedural bones are driven at runtime only: animation clips must never key them.

meshes._doc: Required mesh names (glTF mesh or node name). All are skinned to the single armature. Both eyes share one mesh, each eye weighted 100 % to its eye bone; same for the eyelids. The teeth, the tusks and the mouth each add one: 9 draw calls.

required.name: body
required._doc: Closed, rounded skin. Belly and cheeks lighter via texture.

required.name: face
required._doc: Thin shell over the face carrying the expression atlas (lip line, brows, blush). Cut along the lips like the body and weighted like the skin under it, so its lower part opens with the jaw.

required.name: eyes
required._doc: Two spheres with iris and pupil in the texture. Weighted 100 % to eye_L / eye_R.

required.name: eyelids
required._doc: Upper lids as partial spheres slightly larger than the eyes. Weighted 100 % to eyelid_L / eyelid_R.

required.name: eye_highlights
required._doc: Small unlit quads weighted to head, not to the eyes, so the catchlights stay fixed while the eyes rotate.

required.name: plates
required._doc: Hexagonal dorsal plates along spine and tail. Emissive, driven by a runtime glow uniform.

required.name: teeth
required._doc: T-rex style blade teeth in the gums just inside the lips: the upper row weighted like the upper lip, the lower like the jaw. Hidden while the mouth is closed.

required.name: tusks
required._doc: Two upper tusks hanging over the lower lip and two lower tusks rising over the upper lip, with growth rings, ivory to white. Always shown: they are what the closed mouth shows of the jaw.

required.name: mouth
required._doc: The mouth cavity and tongue behind the lips, coloured by vertex colours: the upper half weighted to head, the lower half and the tongue to jaw.

materials._doc: Required material names. Colours reference colors.* tokens.

textures._doc: Expected images. size is the edge in px per tier (square, power of two); null means the texture is dropped in that tier. AO is baked into the red channel of body_orm.

expressions._doc: Expressions are cells of a 2x2 atlas on the face material, switched by UV offset (texture.offset in three). Cells are [column, row] with row 0 at the top (glTF UV origin). The face mesh UVs are authored inside cell [0, 0]. No morph targets: the mouth opens with the jaw (see jaw), and the atlas carries the lip line, brows and blush.

clips._doc: Required animation clips, baked at fps, no root motion (the root bone is never keyed). Procedural bones (skeleton.procedural) are never keyed. durationS is nominal, checked with durationToleranceS.

required.name: hatch
required._doc: Pops out of the egg shell and settles.

required.name: look_around
required._doc: Idle curiosity, used on touch devices without interaction.

required.name: roar
required._doc: Finale. Pairs with the roar expression.

required.name: jump
required._doc: Small hop on click or tap.

gaze._doc: Look-at layer applied after AnimationMixer.update as a rotation offset on top of the clip pose, never replacing it. Damping is frame-rate independent: x += (target - x) * (1 - exp(-lambda * dt)). Angles are limits relative to the clip pose.

headChain._doc: Total yaw and pitch shared along the chain; shares must add up to 1.

blink._doc: Eyelid geometry is authored open in the bind pose. A positive rotation of closedAngleDeg about the eyelid bone local +X closes it.

life._doc: Secondary motion layered after the gaze. The tail is a damped spring per link, pushed by the hips: turning swings it the other way, rising drops it. Frequency in rad/s, gains in seconds of lag per rad/s (yaw) and per m/s of vertical speed (pitch).

colors._doc: Purple is the accent for the mascot, glows and the CTA only. The UI stays on the monochrome logo palette. Mirrored as Tailwind tokens in src/app/globals.css.

egg._doc: Procedural egg (0 KB of assets): a rounded dinosaur egg, fuller at the bottom (taper), with a shell of embossed polygonal plates, tubercles and speckles computed on the GPU. The page opens on an empty stage; the visitor drops the egg (docs/interaction-script.md): it falls from above the screen with drop.gravity, lands with a squash and bounces (restitution, settling under settleMps), then wobbles and cracks, and hatches when the model is ready and at least minDisplayS has passed since the drop, so it never flickers. radiusM is the widest radius.

jaw._doc: A T-rex style jaw (phase 7, the owner's request): the lips are cut along the mouth line and the lower jaw hinges on the procedural jaw bone, far back like a T-rex's. openDeg is how far each expression opens it; the scroll script opens it further (up to maxOpenDeg) and the bite snaps it shut in biteS. lambda is how fast it follows.

interaction._doc: Kelo alive on one screen (phases 8 and 9, docs/interaction-script.md). Taps within streakS of each other build a streak; each tap plays the reaction for its place in the streak, and on desktop the tap numbered biteAt makes him bite the screen. Past the last reaction, touch devices repeat it, and their tap numbered gameAt opens the pixel runner. A press that moves further than dragThresholdPx is a drag (desktop only). actions are what the desktop sandbox's dock asks of him, played like reactions.

desktop._doc: Dragging and the bite need a fine pointer that can hover, on a screen at least minWidthPx wide.

carry._doc: Being held: the grab point follows the pointer on a critically damped spring (followHz); the body hangs from it like a pendulum (lengthM, dampingRatio), swinging with the hand's sideways acceleration up to maxSwingDeg and leaning with its vertical speed up to maxLeanDeg. Legs dangle and kick, arms rise by armRaiseDeg and flap by armFlapRatio of it on top (at most 50° in all: the rig has no collarbones, and the model build checks the side of the body stays still at that raise), and the body stretches along fast motion.

fall._doc: Let go, he keeps the hand's velocity (up to maxThrowMps): gravity and air drag pull him down, the screen edges bounce him back. On the floor he bounces with restitution, slides to a stop with friction, and squashes to landSquash of his height, springing back at squashHz. marginM keeps him inside the screen.

hop._doc: The single-pointer alternative to dragging: a click on empty floor, or an arrow key with Kelo focused, makes him hop there (arrow keys stepM at a time).

bite._doc: The full-screen bite on the tap numbered taps.biteAt (desktop, no reduced motion): src/lib/live/bite.ts keys it over durationS.

quality._doc: Tier picked at boot from device heuristics, then adjusted at runtime with drei's PerformanceMonitor along a ladder (src/lib/quality/ladder.ts): step up above upperFps, lock after flipflops. Within a tier the render pixel ratio steps down first, below dprLowerFps, from dprMax (or the device's) through dprSteps to dprMin; only then does the tier change, below lowerFps.

accessibility._doc: Applied when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. The scene stays, motion is minimised, and content never depends on the animation.
